clue.text: Setting up Italian agreement, the French give ground

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it, so the Italian word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: si is Italian for yes
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Talks with an Italian end in a deal once the French back down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give ground' looks like a single phrase meaning yield; 'give' is only a link and 'ground' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Land in general can be called ground, and an island is a piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Looking round for a letter?

definitions.meaning: having a round shape or appearance
a letter copied and sent out to many people at once

explanation.surface: Someone peering about in search of a missing letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Round in shape is the plain adjective sense; a printed letter sent to a whole list is the noun sense.

clue.text: Sicilian hothead

parts.note: a hot-tempered islander on the surface, but really the fiery summit of Sicily's volcano

explanation.surface: A quick-tempered man from Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily's famous active volcano has a literally hot head, its erupting crater.

clue.text: On the verge of alarming changes

indicators.note: the letters of the word before are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Things are close to alarming developments.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the edge or border, close to a limit, is marginal; the margin is the verge of a page.

clue.text: Goes through customs at university

parts.note: customs are habits or uses
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student passing through border control at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'customs' suggests the airport check; here it means habitual practices.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through supplies is to consume or exhaust them entirely.

clue.text: Underground movement providing opposition

definitions.meaning: a secret organisation fighting an occupying power, like the French wartime one
the act of pushing back against force

explanation.surface: A secret group that supplies opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret wartime fighters against occupation were called this, and the word also means simply opposing force.

clue.text: About to give way and withdraw

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to cede is to yield or give way

explanation.surface: Someone on the point of yielding and pulling back.
explanation.definitionFit: To move back or retreat, as floodwaters or a hairline do, is a synonym of withdraw.

clue.text: Potato peelers may miss them, if they don't keep them peeled

definitions.text: Potato peelers may miss them, if they don't keep them peeled

parts.words: Potato peelers may miss them, if they don't keep them peeled
parts.note: potatoes have small dark buds that a careless peeler leaves in, and keeping these peeled means watching carefully

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice: a careless potato peeler leaves bits behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The buds on a potato share their name with organs of sight, which you keep peeled when alert.

clue.text: Go around in women's clothing

definitions.meaning: to pass round the edge of something, avoiding it
a garment hanging from the waist

explanation.surface: Going about town dressed as a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to pass round the edge of an obstacle; the noun is a woman's garment worn from the waist.

clue.text: Simply gives us tea when out — depend on it!

indicators.note: out describes the letters as disordered, so they are rearranged

parts.note: to rely is to depend on

explanation.surface: Someone who just hands over tea whenever we are away; count on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Done plainly and without ornament, the adverb sense of simply.

clue.text: Calls may be made via these money markets

definitions.text: Calls may be made via these
definitions.meaning: telephone switching centres route phone calls
places where stocks or currencies are traded

explanation.surface: Phone calls on a trading floor, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calls' looks like a trading term but it means phone calls.
explanation.definitionFit: Telephone switching centres and stock or currency markets share this name.

clue.text: Schemes thrown aside

indicators.note: thrown suggests the letters are tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: Plans that have been discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans or schemes are notions someone has thought up, a synonym in the plural.

clue.text: One with a large bill gets the Spanish into a dreadful panic

indicators.note: into puts the Spanish word inside the rearranged letters
dreadful marks the letters of panic as in a bad state, to be rearranged

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A diner hit with a huge bill finds Spaniards in a frightful panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges the panic letters, and 'into' sets the Spanish article inside; 'bill' suggests money but means a beak.
explanation.definitionFit: This water bird has a huge beak, and a bird's beak is its bill.

clue.text: Beginner in discomfort — that's obvious

indicators.note: in places the learner's letter inside the word for discomfort

parts.note: pain is discomfort
L is a learner, as on British L-plates for learner drivers

explanation.surface: A novice in distress; clear enough.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from British L-plates on learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear and easily seen or understood, as in plain to see.

clue.text: Rags-to-riches story recalled in new adaptation

indicators.note: a new adaptation of a text reworks it, so the letters before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fairy tale remembered in a fresh version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' suggests remembering, but 'recalled in' is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy tale of a mistreated girl who marries a prince is the classic tale of rising from poverty to wealth.

clue.text: One with a complaint but is prepared to wait

definitions.meaning: a person with an illness, a medical complaint, under a doctor's care
describes someone tolerant of delay

explanation.surface: Someone with a grievance who is still willing to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' reads as a grievance, but it means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick person under treatment is the noun sense; being willing to wait calmly is the adjective sense.

clue.text: A writer Kipling never expected to meet

definitions.meaning: Mark ___, the American author of Tom Sawyer
Kipling wrote that East and West, never the ___ shall meet, an old word for the two

explanation.surface: An author Kipling never thought he would meet.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's Ballad of East and West says 'never the twain shall meet', twain being an old word for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain is the pen name of an American author; the word is also old English for two, from Kipling's line.

clue.text: Ideal stage for kitchen-sink drama?

parts.note: a stage that juts out into the audience shares its name with a garment worn at the sink, and kitchen-sink drama is gritty domestic realism

explanation.surface: Which theatre stage best suits gritty domestic realism?
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchen-sink drama is a British term for 1950s-60s plays of working-class home life.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage projecting in front of the curtain carries the name of the garment worn while cooking or washing up.

clue.text: Comfortable place to sit and drink

definitions.meaning: the top of the thighs of a seated person, where a child might sit
to drink as a cat does, with the tongue

explanation.surface: A cosy spot to settle down with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The thighs of someone seated make a seat for a child; a cat drinks milk with its tongue this way.

clue.text: A payment covered by friend of father, perhaps

indicators.note: covered by puts the first pieces inside the word for friend

parts.note: a pal is a friend
rent is a regular payment for a home

explanation.surface: A payment covered by Dad's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friend of father' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'of father, perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a mother or father; father is one example, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Lake in Tanzania included in many a safari

indicators.note: included in signals that the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An African lake that features on many safari tours.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the old name of Lake Malawi, a great lake bordered by Tanzania, Malawi and Mozambique.

clue.text: A woman in Minnesota is likely to be this

definitions.text: A woman in Minnesota is likely to be this

indicators.note: in puts the woman's name inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: MN is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Minnesota
Erica is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman living in Minnesota is most likely a US citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is a US state, so a woman there is probably a US national.

clue.text: At present not there, nor anywhere else

parts.note: now means at present
the opposite of there is here

explanation.surface: Someone currently absent and not to be found anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: In no place at all, so not anywhere, which is the sense of the adverb.

clue.text: Bending elbow with boozer, beginning to sway unsteadily

indicators.note: bending the letters out of shape rearranges them
beginning takes the first letter of the drinker's word

explanation.surface: A drinker bending the elbow starts to sway about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bending elbow' looks like the drinking idiom; 'Bending' rearranges ELBOW with B, the start of 'boozer'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock or move unsteadily from side to side, as a drunk might.

clue.text: An insect from near Wigan

indicators.note: from takes the letters out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bug found near the town of Wigan.
explanation.walkthrough: Wigan is a town in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A small insect with pincers at its tail, said in folklore to creep into ears.

clue.text: Eggs on head of school — it's not for boys

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
a dean heads a college or university faculty

explanation.surface: A headteacher served eggs at a girls-only school.
explanation.walkthrough: Roedean is a famous English girls' boarding school near Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: This English boarding school takes only girls, so it is not for boys.

clue.text: Cut and wound wild bears

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Untamed bears slash and injure.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to strike or wound someone with a curved cavalry sword.

clue.text: Boss upset and shows distress

indicators.note: upset knocks the letters of the word over into a new order

explanation.surface: The boss is upset and showing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying with convulsive gasps is a clear show of distress.

clue.text: Dramatic performance in translation

definitions.meaning: an interpretation of a role or a song
a version in another language

explanation.surface: A stage performance given in translated form.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both performing a piece and rendering a text into another language.

clue.text: Suspect in a short time loses head

indicators.note: loses head drops the first letter of the word

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment, a short time

explanation.surface: A suspect beheaded in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link; 'loses head' removes J.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubtful or questionable, the informal adjective, matches suspect as an adjective.

clue.text: A blue or white flower

definitions.meaning: the two main branches of the great African river are called Blue and White
something that flows, a river

explanation.surface: A flower in blue or white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' reads as a bloom but means a thing that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The African river has Blue and White branches, and a river is a flower in the sense of something that flows.

clue.text: It needs pluck to play in triangular formation

definitions.text: It needs pluck to play in triangular formation

parts.words: It needs pluck to play in triangular formation
parts.note: a Russian stringed instrument with a three-sided body is played by plucking, not by needing courage

explanation.surface: Something needing courage to perform in a triangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pluck' reads as courage but means plucking strings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian folk lute has a triangular body and its strings are plucked.

clue.text: Weak and unable to succeed outright

definitions.meaning: lacking strength, delicate
too feeble to win through fully; the setter also folds out(side) and right into the one word around a verb for falling short

explanation.surface: Feeble and unable to win clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter intends a container: split 'outright' into out (outside) and right (R), wrapped by a verb for falling short. One clue word cannot be both indicator and piece in this parse, so it is shown as two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Physically delicate and lacking strength, too feeble to carry anything through.
